whatIsBehavioral.title: What is a Behavioral Interview?
whatIsBehavioral.description: Behavioral interviews assess how you've handled real situations in the past. The premise is simple: past behavior predicts future behavior. For senior roles, these interviews evaluate leadership qualities, decision-making, and cultural fit.

keyPoints.title: Past Behavior Predicts Future Performance
keyPoints.description: Companies want specific examples of how you've handled challenges, not hypothetical answers about what you 'would' do.

keyPoints.title: More Important at Senior Levels
keyPoints.description: For Directors and VPs, behavioral rounds often carry more weight than technical rounds. Leadership signals matter.

keyPoints.title: Preparation is Everything
keyPoints.description: The best performers don't improvise—they've prepared 15-20 polished stories that can flex to different questions.

starMethod.title: Master the STAR Method
starMethod.subtitle: A proven structure for compelling interview stories
starMethod.description: STAR stands for Situation, Task, Action, Result. This framework ensures your answers are specific, focused, and demonstrate impact. Here's how to use it effectively:

steps.name: Situation
steps.description: Set the context briefly. Who, what, where, when? Keep it to 2-3 sentences maximum.
tips: Be specific—vague situations lead to vague answers

steps.name: Task
steps.description: What was YOUR specific responsibility or challenge? Clarify what you personally needed to accomplish.

steps.name: Action
steps.description: This is 60-70% of your answer. What specific steps did YOU take? Be detailed about your decisions and approach.
tips: Explain your reasoning for key decisions
Don't describe team actions as your own

steps.name: Result
steps.description: What was the outcome? Quantify when possible. Include learnings if relevant.
tips: Use metrics: revenue, time saved, team size, percentages
If the outcome was negative, explain what you learned

amazonLP.title: Amazon Leadership Principles
amazonLP.subtitle: The most rigorous behavioral interviews in tech
amazonLP.description: Amazon's 16 Leadership Principles form the backbone of their interview process. Every question maps to one or more LPs. Understanding this framework is essential for Amazon interviews and valuable for any FAANG company.

principles.name: Customer Obsession
principles.description: Leaders start with the customer and work backwards.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer
Describe a decision you made that was unpopular but right for the customer

principles.name: Ownership
principles.description: Leaders think long-term and don't sacrifice value for short-term results.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you took on something outside your area of responsibility
Describe a time you saw a problem and fixed it without being asked

principles.name: Invent and Simplify
principles.description: Leaders expect innovation from their teams and find ways to simplify.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you found a simple solution to a complex problem
Describe your most innovative idea and how you implemented it

principles.name: Are Right, A Lot
principles.description: Leaders have strong judgment and good instincts.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time your judgment proved correct despite opposition
Describe a decision where you had to make a call with incomplete data

principles.name: Learn and Be Curious
principles.description: Leaders are never done learning and seek to improve themselves.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about something you learned recently that made you better at your job
Describe how you stay current in your field

principles.name: Hire and Develop the Best
principles.description: Leaders raise the performance bar with every hire and promotion.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about your best hire and why they were successful
Describe how you've developed someone on your team

principles.name: Insist on the Highest Standards
principles.description: Leaders continually raise the bar and drive quality.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you refused to compromise on quality
Describe a time you had to improve a team's standards

principles.name: Think Big
principles.description: Leaders create and communicate a bold direction that inspires results.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about your most ambitious goal
Describe a time you proposed a bold vision

principles.name: Bias for Action
principles.description: Speed matters in business. Many decisions are reversible.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you had to make a quick decision
Describe a situation where you took action without waiting for approval

principles.name: Frugality
principles.description: Accomplish more with less. Constraints breed resourcefulness.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you delivered results with limited resources
Describe how you've reduced costs while maintaining quality

principles.name: Earn Trust
principles.description: Leaders listen, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you had to rebuild trust
Describe a difficult conversation you had with a colleague or leader

principles.name: Dive Deep
principles.description: Leaders operate at all levels, stay connected to details.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you caught a problem by looking at the details
Describe how you stay connected to the work when managing large teams

principles.name: Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit
principles.description: Leaders challenge decisions when they disagree, even when uncomfortable.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager
Describe a time you committed to a decision you disagreed with

principles.name: Deliver Results
principles.description: Leaders focus on key inputs and deliver with the right quality and timeliness.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you delivered a difficult project under pressure
Describe your biggest professional accomplishment

principles.name: Strive to be Earth's Best Employer
principles.description: Leaders create safe, productive, empathetic, and fun work environments.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about how you've created an inclusive team environment
Describe how you support work-life balance for your team

principles.name: Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility
principles.description: Leaders make decisions mindful of broader impact on society and the environment.
exampleQuestions: Tell me about a decision where you considered broader societal impact
Describe how you balance business goals with social responsibility

faqs.question: How many stories should I prepare for behavioral interviews?
faqs.answer: Prepare 15-20 strong stories from your career. Each story should be versatile enough to answer multiple types of questions. Focus on stories with clear impact, leadership signals, and learnings. Quality beats quantity—a few well-practiced stories outperform many poorly-prepared ones.

faqs.question: How long should my STAR answers be?
faqs.answer: Aim for 2-3 minutes per answer. Keep Situation and Task brief (30 seconds combined), spend 60-90 seconds on Actions (the meat of your answer), and 20-30 seconds on Results. If you're going past 4 minutes, you're probably including too much detail.

faqs.question: What if I don't have a story that fits the question?
faqs.answer: First, pause and think—you likely have a relevant story but need to find the right angle. If truly stuck, it's okay to adapt a related story: 'I haven't faced that exact situation, but here's a similar challenge...' Never make up stories; interviewers follow up with probing questions.

faqs.question: How do I handle 'Tell me about a failure' questions?
faqs.answer: Choose a real failure with genuine stakes (not a humble-brag disguised as failure). Own your role without excessive blame or excuses. Spend 70% of your answer on what you learned and how you applied those learnings. Demonstrate growth and self-awareness.

faqs.question: Should I use 'I' or 'we' when describing team accomplishments?
faqs.answer: Use 'I' to describe YOUR specific contributions, and 'we' only when describing true team outcomes. Interviewers want to understand what YOU did. Saying 'we built' tells them nothing about your role. Be specific: 'I led the design, coordinated with 3 teams, and personally reviewed all code.'

faqs.question: How do Amazon LP interviews differ from regular behavioral interviews?
faqs.answer: Amazon uses a structured interview system where each interviewer focuses on 2-3 specific Leadership Principles. They ask follow-up questions to probe depth ('Tell me more about X') and test authenticity ('What would you do differently?'). Preparation should map stories to specific LPs, not just general themes.

faqs.question: What if I'm transitioning from IC to management and don't have management stories?
faqs.answer: Leadership isn't just about managing people. Highlight stories where you led projects, mentored teammates, influenced without authority, drove cross-team initiatives, or made decisions that impacted others. These 'informal leadership' experiences are valid and valued.

faqs.question: How do I prepare for executive-level (Director/VP) behavioral interviews?
faqs.answer: Executive interviews focus more on strategic thinking, organizational impact, and leadership philosophy. Prepare stories about building teams, setting vision, navigating organizational complexity, and making decisions with company-wide implications. Numbers should reflect business impact, not just technical metrics.
